title: Anyon Crystallization by Statistics
authors: Zohar Komargodski, Xuzixiang Lou, Ivri Nagar, Domenico Orlando, Susanne Reffert, Amit Sever
abstract: We revisit the long-standing problem of the anyon gas. We study the solvable near-bosonic limit of a large number of anyons $N$ at fixed $N/k$, where $1/k$ characterizes the statistical interaction. In this limit, the ground state is a crystal with order $N/k$ lattice sites. The statistical interactions, mediated by a long-range gauge field, are completely screened within the crystalline phase. The resulting state is a conventional crystal without superfluidity. We characterize this anyon crystal by determining its unit-cell size, ground-state energy, acoustic excitations, angular momentum crossings, and other properties.   Our results indicate a quantum phase transition between the crystal at $k>k_c$ and a superfluid at $k<k_c$, with a critical value $k_c\simeq2\text{--}5$. These results imply that an anyon gas with only statistical interactions is not necessarily a superfluid, contrary to common lore.   We also present a detailed analysis of the renormalization-group evolution of anyon--anyon interactions, identifying many new potential fixed points and elucidating finite-size effects.
summary: This work analyzes the phase diagram of an anyon gas, predicting a quantum phase transition between a crystalline state and a superfluid state. By studying the effective Hamiltonian in the large $k$ limit, the authors determine a critical value $k_c$ that contradicts common assumptions about anyon superfluidity. The findings are significant for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter systems.
main_problem: The paper revisits the long-standing problem of the anyon gas, specifically investigating the quantum phase transition between crystalline and superfluid states.
main_result: The system undergoes a quantum phase transition at a critical parameter $k_c \simeq 2-5$, implying that an anyon gas with only statistical interactions is not necessarily a superfluid.
method: The analysis employs a double-scaling limit, semiclassical saddle-point methods, and Renormalization Group (RG) analysis of the effective Hamiltonian derived from a Chern-Simons action.
model_or_system: The system models anyons (particles with fractional statistics $	heta = \pi/k$) at fixed density $\lambda = N/k$, described by an effective Hamiltonian involving density and phase variables.
key_observables: Unit-cell size, ground-state energy, acoustic excitations, and the critical value $k_c$ separating the two phases.
important_parameters: The statistical parameter $k$, the density parameter $\lambda = N/k$, and the critical value $k_c$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large $k$ limit (semiclassical expansion) and assumes the system is at the infrared-stable fixed point of the RG flow.
figures_summary: Figure 1 (mentioned) shows the sequence of classical saddles found by minimizing the energy functional as a function of the density parameter $\lambda$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by deriving the effective Hamiltonian, analyzing the energy minimization in different density regimes ($\lambda$), and finally establishing the quantum phase transition boundary using RG techniques.
why_interesting: The study of anyons and their phase transitions provides a theoretical framework relevant to strongly correlated electron systems, such as fractional quantum Hall states, which are key topics in condensed matter theory.

(This state is known exactly to all orders in the 1/𝑘expansion, as reviewed in the main body of the paper.) (b) A centered unit-vortex solution. The crystal is screened in the sense that, after coarse-graining over several unit cells, the vortex density approaches the matter density. The unscreened component is depleted in the bulk and survives predominantly near the edge at finite 𝜆.
